recipes.name: Salsa Chicken Rice Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Place rice and water in a saucepan, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, place chicken breast halves into a large saucepan, and fill the pan with water. Bring to a boil, and cook for 20 minutes, or until done. Remove chicken from water. When cool enough to handle, cut meat into bite-size pieces.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.

In a medium bowl, combine Monterey Jack and Cheddar cheeses. In a separate bowl, mix together cream of chicken soup, cream of mushroom soup, onion, and salsa. Layer 1/2 of the rice, 1/2 of the chicken, 1/2 of the soup and salsa mixture, and 1/2 of the cheese mixture in prepared dish. Repeat layers, ending with cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for about 40 minutes, or until bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Salsa Chicken Rice Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Layers of rice, chicken, cheese, and a creamy salsa sauce are baked in an easy, flavorful casserole.

review.reviewBody: I was given this recipe for a semester-long class assignment in which I had to alter the recipe to have 33% less sodium, 33% less calories, and replace the white rice with a whole grain. I did this over 5 weeks, with a different test substitution. The successful substitutions included: brown rice, elimination of the mushroom soup and using a whole can of Campbell's healthy request chicken soup, reducing the cheese by one cup and using a 75% reduced fat cheddar cheese instead of the two types of cheese. The dish continued to be the favorite of the class after each substitution. Hope everyone tries these easy substitutions!

I really liked this recipe! It wasn't too labor intensive and was pretty cheap to make, too! I needed one that I could freeze, and I will definitely make this one again. I did make a good bit of adjustments, though: - I actually didn't use the salsa at all (I don't really love jarred salsa and didn't feel like making my own). Instead, I topped with sour cream and hot sauce (I think next time I'll try a buffalo sauce instead). - shredded a whole rotisserie chicken instead of baking chicken breasts - sautéed the onion before baking, along with 4 cloves of garlic, two large jalapeño peppers (seeds included), and one medium yellow bell pepper. Will probably add another jalapeño pepper and a green bell pepper next time (veggie lover). - substituted Monterey Jack cheese for pepper jack, per another reviewer's suggestion - covered dish with aluminum foil before baking I usually get tired of eating the same thing more than 2 or 3 times in a week (partly why I wanted a freezer friendly meal), but I've already eaten half of it and am nowhere close to sick of it!

From looking at the original recipe, I imagined it would be incredibly bland without any seasoning and cooking everything in plain water. I first seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder before putting it in the crock pot with one box of chicken broth. I cooked it on low for about 2.5 hours and then cut it into chunks with kitchen scissors. I used the chicken broth from the pot to cook the rice and I added about two tablespoons of butter to the rice after it was cooked. I used a big Pyrex dish so I only had enough ingredients for one layer. It came out pretty good. I'd make it again. It wasn't phenomenal but it definitely gets the job done for an easy weeknight meal with enough leftovers to last. Next time, I'll try it with homemade Spanish rice instead and possibly some diced chilis for an extra kick.

I've been using this recipe for about 5-6 years and since the first time I made it I did things a bit differently. Cook chicken breast in skillet. When cool, dice into 1" pieces. Cook 1 and 1/2 cups brown rice in a large pot. Mix cooked chicken and rice. Mix in about 6 oz shredded cheddar, about 4 oz shredded pepper jack, and 2 cans of cream of chicken soup and one can of mild Rotel tomatoes. Mix very well and place in greased/buttered baking dish. 350 oven about 30 minutes. When bubbly, top with another 2oz each of cheddar and pepper jack until all melty. Yum! Basically cooking what needs cooked and then just mixing it all together, No layering, easy and just as tasty!

Made basically as written. Used peach salsa and covered with foil for 30 of the 40 minutes. My husband hates crunchy bits so that's why I covered it. When I put the sauce layer on, I spread it evenly with a spoon to avoid dry spots. I used leftover chicken from the crockpot (taco seasoning/oil/lemon juice/honey). But chicken was drained.

Love the recipe. Made it twice, but I too had to spice it up a little the second time. I made my taco seasoning and rubbed it into the chicken and baked it with fresh mde pineapple salsa. I made homemade spanish rice with corn and black beans. Added all the pineapple salsa and the baked chicken with the cheese and soups, and this time the loved it many many compliments, and a clean casserole dish in the end. Family satisfied and well fed. Thank you so much.

I gave this recipe 5 stars for it's versatility. My family likes heat with their Mexican food and I don't like anything spicy. As written, I thought the recipe looked to bland for us. Here are the changes I made. I used 2 packs of Knorr Spanish Rice. I used 2 cans of Kirkland brand chicken. I sauteed the chicken in olive oil along with onions and green peppers. I combined cream of chicken soup and the salsa and added that to the chicken mixture. Tossed in a can of drained black beans and fire roasted corn. Topped with crushed Doritos and Mexican style cheese. Covered with foil and baked 40 minutes. I omitted the sour cream because I'm lactose intolerant. Hubby and kids added it to theirs. This recipe is a keeper. Thanks for sharing.

I’ve been on a Sunday casserole kick lately in order to give us lunch through the week, and this one makes the cut. I made a couple of modifications...I used a rotisserie chicken (shredded), and I used medium salsa instead of mild. I mixed the soup mixture in with the chicken before spreading. I also made this into more of a “lasagna” by layering flour tortillas in as well. I topped mine with sour cream & my husband topped his with guacamole, and we both had a few pickled jalapeños and a side of blue corn chips. Our son ate it as-is with a side of chips. It seemed to be lacking just a little bit of freshness, but I’m not sure what else I would change to bring that to the dish...maybe top with lettuce & tomato. All in all, I think this one will be added to our Sunday casserole rotation.

Oh my goodness! You have GOT to try this recipe - it made a wonderful dinner. Even my picky eaters loved it. This was really delicious. And easy! I did make one change: put the rice and water in the pan first, uncooked after preparing the chicken (because I wanted to use only one pan). I added 35 minutes to cooking time to make sure all the water was absorbed by the rice (timed to make sure rice was fully cooked). But otherwise, I followed the recipe faithfully - Added my own fresh salsa recipe on top when serving (onion, tomato, cilantro, seeded jalapeno, and a pinch of cumin), and added a side of steamed broccoli, and a good meal was had by all.

4 stars with revisions.
Just reading the recipe and then the reviews, it was clear this recipe was far too bland and tasteless for my family, but it had potential. I used hot salsa, (may try spicy green instead of red next time), and at least a tablespoon of garlic and a teaspoon of cumin. I didn't have it, but next time I'll replace the mushroom soup with a 1/2 or full cup of Mexican crema. I chopped up pickled jalapenos and sprinkled them on top. It was very tasty, and worth making again. I also think that next time I'll sprinkle taco seasoning over the rice before putting the chicken in.

I made this with using 3 & 1/2 cups cooked minute rice and sautéed raw chicken cubes with onions. I seasoned the chicken with onion and garlic powder, salt and pepper, and Cumin and Chili Powder. I followed the rest of the recipe as written. Had I boiled the chicken and not seasoned it, I think this recipe would be very bland as others have stated. I will make it again and add a sautéed green pepper and some cooked bacon. I think it would be fabulous!
Needs some diced green chilies or possibly jalapeño to give a stronger southwest vibe.
I don't layer it, I just cook the rice then mix it all and save part of the cheese for the top

I made it following most of the recipe…except I used Rotel instead of salsa, thighs instead of breast and added a chopped japaleno with the onion. I also sprinkled Cajun seasoning in with the soup/Rotel mixture.

I liked it but I altered the recipe too. I added chicken bouillon to the water when I boiled the chicken, then I added a good medium salsa and I also added a 1/4 cup of taco seasoning and some Tajin seasoning for its lime flavor. I used jasmine rice and I didn't add anything to it. I served this dish with white corn tortilla chips, sliced tomatoes, green onions and avacado. Also, I placed some hot sauce on the table for additional heat. My family enjoys spicy food.
Followed the recipe exactly and it’s incredibly bland. Would not make again.
It was easy and great for all ages
Liked the flavors mixed together. Tastes even better the next day! A great way to use leftover chicken.

I used two cream of chicken soups as I didn’t have cream of mushroom and the grandkids are not fond of mushrooms. If you have the bowls/ measuring cups I found it helpful to measure the layers as I made 1.5 the recipe one time and doubled it the other. Have made it several times now using white or brown rice and with mild and medium salsa. A winner every time and the whole family enjoyed the meal. It’s in the rotation!

This was a simple , easy and affordable recipe using household staples! I didn't use white rice, I used brown instead for a healthiest option. I purchased corn tortillas chips and taco sauce for those who wanted an extra kick! Family smash hit and added into recipe rotation! 5 Stars!
